$comment: An entry here is a DOCUMENTED RISK ACCEPTANCE, not a suppression. Each one
must state why no patched version can be adopted, what limits the exposure,
and when the acceptance expires. scripts/check-dependency-audit.mjs fails the
build when an entry expires, when an allowlisted advisory stops appearing
(stale entry must be deleted), or when any advisory outside this file reaches
HIGH or CRITICAL in the production tree.

accepted.why_unpatched: Reached only via @huggingface/transformers@4.2.0, which pins sharp ^0.34.5. 4.2.0 is the latest published release, so no upgrade exists; npm reports fixAvailable=false.
exposure_assessment: sharp is a Node-only image codec used by the transformers Node backend.
FinPlan Pro loads transformers exclusively in the browser (src/engines/AIEngine.ts dynamic import), where onnxruntime-web is used and sharp is never resolved.
Verified 2026-07-29: after `npm run build`, no dist/assets/*.js references sharp or onnxruntime-node, so the vulnerable code is not shipped to users.
The CVEs require decoding attacker-controlled images through libvips; the product performs no server-side image decoding.
accepted.mitigation: Keep the AI feature browser-only. Do not add a Node/server path that imports @huggingface/transformers without re-reviewing this acceptance.

accepted.summary: Flagged solely because it depends on the vulnerable sharp/onnxruntime-node versions above
accepted.why_unpatched: 4.2.0 is the latest published version; the advisory is inherited from its dependency pins, not from its own code.
exposure_assessment: Same chain as the sharp entry: the vulnerable transitive packages are Node-only and absent from the browser bundle.
onnxruntime-node's adm-zip advisory is resolved separately by the adm-zip ^0.6.0 override in package.json.
accepted.mitigation: Re-evaluate on the next @huggingface/transformers release; drop this entry if the pins move.
